title: intent edit wp <thread>/<seq> --path returns the parent thread's file at rc=0, where it refused a week ago
body:
**MEASURED 2026-09-09 by ic against the shipped pair, while measuring `AC-17.6` before hv ruled on it. This is a REGRESSION and the direction is the bad one: a loud refusal became a silent wrong answer.**

```
intent edit wp ST0064/01 --path   ->  rc=0   /Users/matts/.../intent/st/ST0064/info.md
intent edit wp ST0056/17 --path   ->  rc=0   /Users/matts/.../intent/st/ST0056/info.md
intent edit st ST0056    --path   ->  rc=0   /Users/matts/.../intent/st/ST0056/info.md    <- IDENTICAL to the line above
```

**`0153` RECORDS THE SAME COMMAND REFUSING ON 2026-08-30** -- ``error: `ST0064/01` is neither an address nor an artefact id`` at rc=1. Today it succeeds and hands back the PARENT THREAD's file. **`intent/st/ST0064/WP/01/info.md` EXISTS ON DISK**, so the correct answer is present and a different one is returned.

**THE VERB FULLY RESOLVES THE WORK PACKAGE AND THEN DISCARDS IT.** This is not a truncated id arriving at the resolver -- two controls prove the seq survives the walk:

```
intent edit wp ST0056/99 --path   ->  error: ST0056 has no WP-99          <- the SEQ is validated
intent edit wp ST9999/17 --path   ->  error: no steel thread ST9999       <- the THREAD is validated
```

So both components reach the resolver, both are checked, and the emitted path is the thread's. **The defect is in realisation, not in parsing and not in resolution** -- which is a third place, and neither of the two candidates anyone had named.

**WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE REFUSAL IT REPLACED.** A caller doing `intent edit wp <spec> --path` and opening the result edits the THREAD while believing they are editing the work package. rc=0 and a real, existing file is the pair that defeats every caller-side check: there is no error to notice and no missing path to trip on. The refusal `0153` recorded was safe precisely because it was useless.

**THE ADDRESS GRAMMAR AGREES WITH THE OUTCOME AND SAYS SO OUT LOUD.** `0153`'s other arm has also changed, and the new error names the cause:

```
intent edit wp intent:///threads/ST0064/wps/01 --path
  rc=1  error: `intent:///threads/ST0064/wps/01` has trailing segments after a complete address
        remedy: an address ends at the entity it names; use `?format=` for a representation
```

**_An address ends at the entity it names_, and a work package is not one.** `/threads/ST0064` is the complete address; `wps/01` is trailing junk. So the model does not admit a WP as an addressable entity, and `edit --path` papers over that by answering about the nearest thing that is one.

**THE SAME SHAPE IS IN THE BROWSER PATH GRAMMAR, READ FROM SOURCE.** `intentsvcs/src/nav.rs`: `View::path()` renders `Item` as `/{kind}/{id}` and `View::parse()` matches at most three segments (`[kind, id, field]` -> `Children`), `_ => None`. `form::face_for` declares three kinds -- `thread`, `wp`, `issue` -- so `wp` IS a declared kind, and `View::Item { kind: "wp", id: "ST0056/17" }` renders to `/wp/ST0056/17`, which parses back as ``Children { kind: "wp", id: "ST0056", field: "17" }``. **It does not round-trip and it does not refuse**, which contradicts `parse`'s own docstring: _a spelling that names nothing is refused as a spelling, never resolved to something near it._ **HONEST LIMIT: that paragraph is read from source, not executed. I have not run `View::parse` on that input.** The `edit --path` behaviour above IS driven.

**AND THE CONTRACT TEST CANNOT EXHIBIT IT.** `intentsvcs/tests/nav_is_the_shared_path_contract.rs::every_view_round_trips_through_its_path` is held over `every_view()`, whose docstring says it runs _over the corpus rather than over three hand-picked examples_. It enumerates KINDS from the real declaration and then hard-codes **`id: "ST0056"` for every one of them**, including `wp`. The kind axis is a corpus; the id axis is one literal with no slash in it. **A green here is evidence that ids without separators round-trip, never that ids do** -- the sample cannot exhibit the failure, so the test could not have caught this and cannot catch it now.

**SCOPE OF A FIX, MEASURED RATHER THAN ESTIMATED.** A `View` variant able to carry a compound or nested id touches 11 exhaustive-match sites across 6 files in 2 crates -- `intentsvcs/src/nav.rs`, `intent-cli/src/{render.rs, tui/nav.rs, tui/views.rs, tui/app.rs}` -- plus the contract test, which needs a compound-id arm before it can hold the property. **The TUI arm is NOT a separable arm**: it matches the same enum, so it cannot be deferred or descoped.

**RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING FILINGS.** `0153` is the same territory and its recorded measurement no longer reproduces -- it should not be closed on this, but it should not be read as current either. `0149`'s recorded symptom is ALSO gone (`intent edit issue 148 --path` now refuses correctly, naming realisation rather than a phantom thread). Both were filed against a door that has since moved; this is what the door does now.

**Owed by `WP-17` piece 3 (the realisers), which is where `0149` also parks it.**
